newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu denies praising rebel chief.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu denies praising rebel chief.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko denied hailing rebel leader Laurent Kabila as a "patriot", state television said on Monday.
"Some foreign radio stations claimed this morning that President Mobutu Sese Seko has praised Laurent Kabila and described him as a patriot," the television said.

"The president's office has made this clarification. Those who know President Mobutu know that such a statement does not ressemble him and that he cannot praise a compatriot who has taken up arms in league with our aggressors to hit his own country," it added.
In an interview published by the South African Sunday Times and conducted at his presidential residence in Kinshasa last week, Mobutu urged Kabila to negotiate peace.

"Kabila is a nationalist patriot. I urge him to come to the table with his Zairean brothers and sisters to restore peace in the country and to contribute to the achievement of the current democratic process," Mobutu was quoted as saying.

The interview was published as Zaire's warring parties began their first direct talks on ending six months of civil war in which Kabila's forces have taken more than a third of Zaire. No breakthrough has emerged from the talks in South Africa.

"As head of state Marshal Mobutu has repeatedly said that Laurent Kabila should join his Zairean brothers and sisters around a negotiating table in order to find a peaceful end to the war which is raging in Zaire," the television added.
